title: Switching bound for depth-2 circuits
statement:
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function on $n\ge 1$ variables that is computed by some Boolean circuit of depth at most $2$, size at most $s$, and fan-in at most $w$, where $w\ge 1$. Fix a real parameter $p$ with $0<p\le \tfrac{1}{40w}$ (so in particular $p\le 1$), and draw a random restriction $\rho$ in which each of the $n$ variables is, independently, left free with probability $p$ and otherwise fixed to the value $0$ or to the value $1$, each with probability $\tfrac{1-p}{2}$. Write $f_\rho$ for the restriction of $f$ by $\rho$ (the function $x\mapsto f$ evaluated at the assignment agreeing with $\rho$ on its fixed coordinates and with $x$ on the free ones), and let $D(g)$ denote the least depth of a decision tree computing a function $g$. Then for every $t\in\bbn$,
\[
  \Pr_{\rho}\!\left[\, D(f_\rho) > t \,\right]\ \le\ \left(\tfrac12\right)^{t} + \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{np}{3}\right).
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is computed by a Boolean circuit of depth ≤ 2
replaced:
If $f$ is computed by a circuit of depth at most $2$, size at most $s$, and fan-in at most $w$,
then for a Bernoulli parameter $p$ with $0<p\le 1/(40w)$ and $p\le 1$,
\[
  \Pr_{p}\!\left[\mathrm{dtDepth}(\mathrm{restrictFn}\,f\,\rho) > t\right]

\]
